title: Automation workflow
covers: n8n and similar workflows, scheduled jobs and scripts that read, change or send things in business systems (mail, CRM, shop, calendar).

stakeholders.who: The person whose mailbox, CRM or shop the automation acts on
cares_about: nothing goes out or changes without their say-so
it keeps working when nobody is watching
would_notice: an e-mail that reached a real customer during testing
a record changed that should not have been
no way to see what ran yesterday

stakeholders.who: The customer or colleague who receives what the automation sends
cares_about: one correct message, addressed to them
a message that reads like a person wrote it
would_notice: a message in the wrong language or from an unknown sender

stakeholders.who: Whoever monitors the automation and fixes it when it fails
cares_about: knowing which step failed and why
credentials kept out of the workflow
would_notice: an API key pasted into a node

first_ten_seconds: Is the workflow inactive or in dry-run until the owner approves it?
Read one message it produced, exactly as the recipient would see it: does it read right?
Open the canvas or the script: can you tell from the step names alone what happens?

checks.claim: The automation stays inactive (or in dry-run) until the owner approves going live.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read back the active flag or schedule of every workflow and trigger after import or deploy.
checks.evidence_required: The active state read back from the platform.

source.quote: Imported/new workflows stay inactive until the owner approves activation.

checks.claim: Test and live are separated: test webhooks, test recipients and sandbox accounts are used until approval, and no real customer is reached during testing.
checks.how_to_inspect: List every outbound target (e-mail address, webhook URL, account) used in the test runs.
checks.evidence_required: That list, showing only test targets.

checks.claim: Outreach and bulk sends are created as drafts until the owner explicitly approves sending.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run the flow once with test input and check that the result lands as a draft, not in the sent folder or outbox.
checks.evidence_required: The draft id or a screenshot, and the empty sent log.

source.quote: Outreach drafted only / no auto-send / no bulk

checks.claim: A retry, a double trigger or a re-run creates no second e-mail, record or charge.
checks.how_to_inspect: Trigger the same input twice, retry one failed step, and count the side effects.
checks.evidence_required: The two runs and the count of messages or records (one).

source.quote: Idempotent writes (no duplicate side effects on retry)

checks.claim: Every message a person receives was rendered with realistic test data and read: no 'undefined', 'null', raw {{ }} placeholders, wrong names, broken characters or wrong language.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run the flow with a complete and an incomplete test record (for example without a first name) and read both results in the real mail client or channel.
checks.evidence_required: Both rendered messages, as a screenshot or text.

checks.claim: A failed step retries with backoff and then lands where a person will see it (error workflow, dead-letter, alert); nothing fails silently.
checks.how_to_inspect: Make one external call fail (a wrong URL or a mocked 500) and follow where the failure ends up.
checks.evidence_required: The failed execution and the alert or dead-letter entry it produced.

checks.claim: A real test execution with realistic input ran from start to end; passing validation alone does not count.
checks.how_to_inspect: Execute the workflow manually with test data and keep the execution log.

checks.claim: Credentials sit in the platform's credential store or env, never in node parameters, code steps or exported JSON.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the exported workflow or script for key, token, password and secret.
checks.evidence_required: The search output on the export.

source.quote: Credentials live in n8n credential store / env — never hardcoded in nodes.

checks.claim: The owner can see what ran, when, for whom, and what it sent or changed.
checks.how_to_inspect: Open the execution history or log after a test run and check that it answers those four questions.
checks.evidence_required: A screenshot or excerpt of the log entry.

checks.claim: A webhook-triggered flow answers the caller first and does the slow work afterwards, so the caller never times out.
checks.how_to_inspect: Call the test webhook and time the response while a slow step runs.

checks.claim: Every step has a name that says what it does ('Send booking confirmation'), and the flow reads in one direction.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read the step names only and try to tell the story of the flow without opening any step.
checks.evidence_required: The steps renamed, with old and new names.

source.rationale: The operator debugging a failed run reads step names, not the canvas; 'HTTP Request3' costs them the time the author saved.

checks.claim: Calls to other services respect their rate limits and quotas, with waits or batching where needed.
checks.how_to_inspect: Check the documented limit of each called service against the number of calls one run makes.
checks.evidence_required: The limit per service and the calls per run.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: 'Hi undefined,' or a literal {{ $json.firstName }} in a customer's inbox
the same confirmation arrives twice after a retry
a real customer received a test e-mail
the run failed at step 4 and nobody was told
